thread:
Maya (Support): urgent — ACME (priority tier) reported a big p99 spike right after the 09:00 deploy. Customer on dedicated pool dc-priority-1. They see user-facing latency p95 ~2.6s, p99 ~3.2s for text-generation routes, starting at 09:03. Errors are low (502 ~0.5%) but latency is unacceptable. Can we triage?

Jonas (eng-sre): looking. Graphs show attach/warmup queue rising at 09:01 and GPU utilization at 100% on that pool. Also many "container start" times jumped. Suspect warmup/cold-gpu ramp + image pulls.

Priya (eng-platform): I see a burst of ImagePullBackOff events in eu-central for the priority pool around 09:00 — registry throttling + node disk pressure on 3 nodes. kube events:
```
Warning  Failed     2m (x6 over 4m)  kubelet, ip-10-0-1-23  Failed to pull image "redwood-runtime:v2.4.1": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = denied: quota exceeded
```
That delays container ready, so requests queue up and hit fallback/backpressure.

Alex (oncall): can we fallback traffic for ACME to the eu-west spare pool while we stabilize? Quick mitigation: route their traffic to dedicated-fallback-eu-west until warmups finish.

Maya (Support): Customer is on a live demo in 30m. We need immediate mitigation + postmortem. Mateo is coordinating with ACME.

Mateo (cust-success): I've told ACME we are investigating and offered to failover traffic; they want minimal data residency impact — prefer eu-central if possible. If we must move, get them consent first.

Jonas (eng-sre): mitigation plan I can run now: 1) bump min-ready for dc-priority-1 by +2 GPUs to reduce cold starts, 2) trigger proactive warmup for the busiest model shards, 3) requeue pending attach requests with a randomized backoff. Commands:
```bash
# increase pool min-capacity
redwoodctl pools update dc-priority-1 --min-gpus 6
# trigger warmup for model x
redwoodctl warmup trigger --pool dc-priority-1 --model sales-conv-v1 --concurrency 8
```
I'll also mark the registry as throttled so platform knows to switch image mirror.

Priya (eng-platform): rolling image mirror fallback to internal-cache enabled. Also flagged nodes with diskpressure to cordon/drain and spin fresh nodes. Starting parallel node replacement.

deploy-bot: Deploy v2.4.1 completed at 08:59. Canary passed. No immediate errors flagged.

Alex (oncall): Immediate action I'm taking now: 1) enable route fallback for ACME to eu-west (will message customer), 2) temporarily raise per-customer rate limit to ease backpressure for warmup traffic, 3) run a targeted warmup job to populate KV caches.

Maya (Support): please confirm when route is switched so I can update ACME.

Priya (eng-platform): route switch prepared — running:
```bash
# devops api
curl -XPOST "https://control-plane/api/route/switch" -d '{"customer":"acme","target_pool":"dedicated-fallback-eu-west","ttl":1800}'
```
Response: 200 OK. Traffic steering in progress (~30s). @Alex please verify from control-plane UI.

Alex (oncall): confirmed, traffic for ACME is 85% on fallback now. p99 on customer requests decreased from 3.2s -> 1.1s for a subset of requests. :thumbsup:

Jonas (eng-sre): warmup tasks completed on priority pool, image mirror warmed. GPU attach latency p95 back to baseline but there's a tail for a small fraction of pods that hit registry fallback earlier. I'll keep monitoring queue length and set an alert to auto-bump min-gpus on future bursts.

Priya (eng-platform): root cause summary: registry throttling + transient node disk pressure during a high-concurrency canary led to prolonged image pulls -> delayed container readiness -> attach queue spike -> p99 latency regression. Mitigations applied: image mirror fallback, auto node replacement, proactive warmup job, temporary routing fallback for ACME.

Maya (Support): customer updated. ACME accepted eu-west fallover for the demo window. They reported the UI snappy after the switch.

Mateo (cust-success): ACME asked for postmortem and permanent mitigation. I'll draft customer-facing summary after we finalize internal RCA.

Jonas (eng-sre): Next steps for postmortem: - add registry throttling metric to deployment checklist - implement graceful image prefetch for dedicated pools (pre-pull on scale events) - implement automatic min-gpu increase when attach queue > threshold - refine alerting to correlate imagePullBackOff spikes with attach queue growth.

Priya (eng-platform): I'll add a short-term automation to pre-pull runtime images on pool scale events and a longer-term plan to use multi-registry mirrors.

Maya (Support): thanks all. Closing loop: ACME happy for now; we'll schedule a postmortem and follow-ups. Leaving p99 monitor on until EOD. :eyes:

Jonas (eng-sre): logging action items in the incident board. tagging: @incidents, @eng-platform.

Alex (oncall): Pushed playbook note to runbook: "priority-customer fallover + warmup". Copy of immediate command snippets in playbook.

Mateo (cust-success): I'll follow up with ACME tomorrow and include mitigation timeline.

Maya (Support): great work. :heart:
